page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.16xlarge is an arm64-based general-purpose server instance powered by a 64-core Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this instance allocates dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading, ensuring consistent compute performance. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 114,463.22 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 413.03 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,790.0 and a weaker single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.01 GB/sec. Memory performance is highly efficient for small cached blocks, reaching a read-only bandwidth of 4,547.11 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write speeds average 174.2 GB/sec and 77.47 GB/sec respectively. The instance also demonstrates high efficiency in Redis SET operations, achieving 82.33 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6r.16xlarge leverages the ARM architecture to deliver high core density and strong multi-threaded performance at a lower resource-overhead profile compared to traditional x86 alternatives. However, workloads requiring advanced vector extensions (AVX) or specialized hardware acceleration will face limitations due to the lack of AVX support and dedicated GPUs. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and moderate scale-out workloads such as containerized microservices and distributed data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.16xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by a 64-core Ampere Altra processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 256 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a balanced 4 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. It features a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks highlight strong multi-core capabilities, including a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 413.03 GB/sec and 82.33 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core performance remains average. Additionally, it delivers a static web serving throughput of 33.73 GB/sec and handles medium-sized 7B LLM inference at 21.03 text generation tokens per second. The ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient profile for highly parallelized workloads, making this instance well-suited for multi-threaded applications, web serving, Redis caching, and containerized microservices.
